rule_level_problems.problem: Waist threshold 80 cm applied to all patients; the male threshold (94 cm) is lost, giving false GORD likely in men with waist 80-93 cm.
The page defines 'shock likely' (SBP<80, pulse>=100, RR>30, confusion/restlessness, weakness); no rule derives Shock, so the Urgent item 'Shock' depends on a clinician recording Shock directly.
Fires for every adult with nausea/vomiting, men included; no sex restriction even though 'Female' (finding) exists in SNOMED.
'In cholera outbreak area in past 5 days' is encoded as exposure to Vibrio cholerae with an onset window; onset is the recording time, so the 5-day test does not measure time since being in the area.
'No stools or flatus' approximated by Obstipation OR (Constipation AND no Passing flatus); 'Unable to break wind' (finding) exists and is closer.

summary: The red box is well covered: all 14 urgent criteria and the five 'likely' diagnoses are encoded and wired into one Urgent rule. The most consequential error is the GORD rule's single 80 cm waist threshold, which drops the 94 cm male cut-off. Also missing: the footnote definition of 'shock likely', the medication cause and a sex restriction on 'exclude pregnancy'. The cholera outbreak-area window and 'no stools or flatus' are only approximated.
